units: Lengths are millimetres, angles degrees, mass kilograms, everywhere, whatever the document's own units. Field names carry the unit (value_mm, mass_kg).

errors.BAD_REQUEST: the arguments do not match the tool's schema
errors.SW_NOT_RUNNING: no SOLIDWORKS is running in the Windows desktop session
errors.SW_BUSY: SOLIDWORKS is busy or showing a dialog
errors.TIMEOUT: the call did not finish within its budget
errors.NO_ACTIVE_DOC: no document is active and none was named
errors.DOC_NOT_OPEN: the named document is not open
errors.WRONG_DOC_TYPE: the tool does not apply to this document type
errors.FILE_NOT_FOUND: the path does not exist on the Windows machine
errors.OPEN_FAILED: SOLIDWORKS refused to open the file
errors.PATH_DENIED: the path is outside the folders the bridge may write
errors.FILE_EXISTS: the target exists and overwrite was not requested
errors.SAVE_FAILED: SOLIDWORKS refused to write the file
errors.SAVE_DISABLED: saving over source documents is turned off
errors.DIRTY: the document has unsaved changes the bridge will not discard
errors.MEMBER_MISSING: the API member does not exist on this SOLIDWORKS version
errors.COM_NULL: SOLIDWORKS returned nothing where an object was expected
errors.NOT_CONNECTED: no bridge is connected to dsh

tools.name: sw_status
tools.description: Connection check and session overview. Call this first. Returns the SOLIDWORKS release the bridge is attached to (e.g. 2016 SP1), every SOLIDWORKS instance in the Windows desktop session, the open documents and which one is active. Pass pid to switch to another instance.

pid.description: Attach to the SOLIDWORKS process with this id instead of the one in front.

tools.name: sw_open
tools.description: Open a part (.sldprt), assembly (.sldasm) or drawing (.slddrw) in SOLIDWORKS and make it the active document. Opens read-only unless read_only is false, so edits stay in memory and the file on disk cannot change. Paths are Windows paths on the SOLIDWORKS machine. A document that is already open is activated, not reopened. Large assemblies can take minutes.

read_only.description: Default true. false only when the edits must later be saved over the file.

configuration.description: Configuration to open in; default is the one last saved.

tools.name: sw_new
tools.description: Create a new, empty part or assembly from SOLIDWORKS' default template (or the template given) and make it the active document. It has no file until sw_save gives it a path. Model a part with sw_build; put saved parts together with sw_assemble.

template.description: Windows path of a .prtdot or .asmdot template. Default: the one set in SOLIDWORKS' options.

tools.name: sw_inspect
tools.description: One-call summary of a document: type, file, document units, configurations and the active one, material, custom properties (file-level and active configuration), bounding box in mm, and counts (solid bodies, components). sw_features lists the features. doc defaults to the active document.

doc.description: Path, file name or title of an open document. Default: the active document.

tools.name: sw_features
tools.description: The FeatureManager tree in order: each feature's name, type, suppression state, and its rebuild error if it has one, with sketches nested under the features that use them. Folders and scene items are left out unless include_folders is true.

doc.description: Path, file name or title of an open document. Default: the active document.

offset.description: Skip this many top-level features. Default 0.

limit.description: At most this many top-level features. Default 200.

include_folders.description: Also list folders, lights and other non-modeling entries. Default false.

tools.name: sw_parameters
tools.description: The values that drive the model: every dimension (full name like D1@Sketch1, value in mm or degrees, whether it is driven) and every equation, with global variables marked. Use the names returned here in sw_edit.

doc.description: Path, file name or title of an open document. Default: the active document.

limit.description: At most this many dimensions. Default 500.

tools.name: sw_components
tools.description: The component tree of an assembly: instance name, file, referenced configuration, suppression state, fixed or floating, and position in mm. depth 1 lists top-level components only.

doc.description: Path, file name or title of an open assembly. Default: the active document.

depth.description: Levels of sub-assemblies to expand. Default 1.

limit.description: At most this many components in total. Default 500.

tools.name: sw_mass_properties
tools.description: Mass (kg), volume (mm3), surface area (mm2), density (kg/m3) and centre of mass (mm) of a part or assembly in its active configuration, using the materials assigned in SOLIDWORKS.

doc.description: Path, file name or title of an open part or assembly. Default: the active document.

tools.name: sw_probe
tools.description: Look at specific geometry in a part or assembly. With at: the face, edge or vertex at each model-space point [x, y, z] in mm (a point on an edge picks the edge, on a corner the vertex). Without at: whatever the user has selected in SOLIDWORKS right now, so you can work on what they point at. Faces report their surface type, area, normal or axis and diameter, and the feature that made them; edges report length, ends, centre and diameter. For exactly two entities, also the distance between them and the angle between their directions.

doc.description: Path, file name or title of an open part or assembly. Default: the active document.

at.description: Up to 8 model-space points in mm. Omit to read the user's selection.

tools.name: sw_edit
tools.description: Change a document in memory, then rebuild once. Applies, in this order: configuration (activate), suppress, unsuppress, variables (global variables, by name, as expressions), dimensions (by full name, value in the dimension's own unit: mm or degrees), properties (custom properties). Returns every change with its before and after value, and the rebuild result. Nothing is written to disk; use sw_save or sw_export for that.

doc.description: Path, file name or title of an open document. Default: the active document.

variables.description: Global variable name -> new expression as a string, e.g. {"Width": "60"} or {"Width": "\"Height\" / 2"}.

dimensions.description: Dimension full name -> new value as a number, in mm (lengths) or degrees (angles), e.g. {"D1@Sketch1": 60}.

dimension_scope.description: Apply dimension values to the active configuration only (default) or to all configurations.

properties.description: Custom property name -> text value. Created if missing.

property_scope.description: File-level properties (default) or the active configuration's.

rebuild.description: Rebuild after the changes. Default true.

tools.name: sw_build
tools.description: Model a part: run steps in order on a part, e.g. sketch a profile, extrude it, cut a hole, fillet the edges. Every coordinate is a model-space point [x, y, z] in mm, the space sw_probe and box_mm use: Y is up, the front plane is z = 0, top is y = 0, right is x = 0. So a 12 mm plate on the top plane has its top face at y = 12, and a hole in its middle is centred at [0, 12, 0]. Sketch points off the sketch plane are projected onto it. Faces and edges are picked by a point on them. With atomic (default) a failing step removes what this call made. Returns every feature made with its dimensions, which sw_edit can change later, and the part's volume and bounding box: compare them with what you meant to make.

doc.description: Path, file name or title of an open part. Default: the active document.

name.description: Name for the feature the step makes; a name already in the part is refused before anything is made.

on.description: sketch, plane: front, top, right (in any language's template), or a plane's name. Default front.

face_at.description: sketch: a point on the flat face to sketch on, instead of on.

type.description: centerline: construction line, the axis of a revolve.

through.description: arc: any point on the arc between from and to.

closed.description: polyline: join the last point to the first. Default true.

opposite.description: rectangle: the opposite corner. Edges run along the sketch's axes: the model axes on front, top and right, and on faces parallel to them.

entities.description: sketch: what to draw. Each closed loop becomes a profile; loops inside loops make holes.

sketch.description: extrude, revolve: the sketch to use. Default: the last one this call drew.

depth.description: extrude: mm; with mid_plane the total, centred on the sketch.

cut.description: extrude, revolve: remove material instead of adding it.

reverse.description: extrude, revolve: go the other way. An extrude goes along the sketch normal (out of a face it was sketched on). A cut that would remove nothing that way is made the other way, and the step says reversed.

draft.description: extrude: draft angle in degrees; negative drafts outward.

merge.description: extrude: join the existing body. Default true.

angle.description: revolve: degrees, default 360; the sketch needs one centerline as the axis. chamfer: degrees, default 45.

edges_at.description: fillet, chamfer: a point on each edge, best its middle.

faces_at.description: fillet, chamfer: a point on each face whose edges to round. shell: a point on each face to remove (none: a closed hollow).

outward.description: shell: add the wall outside the current faces. Default false.

offset.description: plane: mm from the plane in on; negative goes the other side.

features.description: delete: names of features sw_build made in this bridge session; nothing else can be deleted, and a sketch of the user's that one of them consumed stays. A delete cannot be undone, so with atomic it is the call's only step.

steps.description: Up to 60 steps, run in order.

atomic.description: Default true: if a step fails, undo this call's earlier steps.

tools.name: sw_study
tools.description: Design study: try up to 50 variants of a model's dimensions and global variables in one call. Each variant is applied, rebuilt and measured (mass, volume, surface area, centre of mass, size, rebuild problems); afterwards every value is put back and checked. Use it to find a value that meets a target, e.g. the wall thickness that keeps mass under 0.2 kg. The document ends unchanged but marked modified.

doc.description: Path, file name or title of an open part or assembly. Default: the active document.

label.description: A name for the variant in the results.

dimensions.description: Dimension full name -> value in mm or degrees, e.g. {"D1@Boss-Extrude1": 30}.

tools.name: sw_rebuild
tools.description: Rebuild a document and report what is wrong: every feature with a rebuild error or warning and the reason. ok is false when any feature fails, even if the rebuild itself ran.

doc.description: Path, file name or title of an open document. Default: the active document.

force.description: Rebuild every feature (Ctrl+Q) instead of only what changed. Default true.

tools.name: sw_assemble
tools.description: Build an assembly: run steps in order on an open assembly (sw_new type assembly makes one). insert adds a saved part or sub-assembly with its origin at a point in mm; the first one is fixed in place unless fixed is false. mate constrains two references: a component's plane, the assembly's plane, or the face, edge or vertex at a point in assembly space. fix and float hold or free a component. Steps before a failing one stay. Returns every component with its origin in mm and the rebuild result, which names mates that fail; check positions with sw_components or sw_view.

doc.description: Path, file name or title of an open assembly. Default: the active document.

steps.description: Up to 60 steps, run in order.

path.description: insert: Windows path of a .sldprt or .sldasm file.

configuration.description: insert: the configuration to use. Default: the file's active one.

at.description: insert: where the component's origin goes, mm. Default [0, 0, 0].

fixed.description: insert: fix it in place. Default true for the assembly's first component, else false.

component.description: A component's name, e.g. bracket-1, for its plane.

plane.description: front, top, right or a plane's name: the component's, or the assembly's without component.

at.description: Instead of plane: a point in assembly space, mm, on the face (or edge, vertex) to mate.

kind.description: With at: what to pick. Default face.

component.description: A component's name, e.g. bracket-1, for its plane.

plane.description: front, top, right or a plane's name: the component's, or the assembly's without component.

at.description: Instead of plane: a point in assembly space, mm, on the face (or edge, vertex) to mate.

kind.description: With at: what to pick. Default face.

align.description: mate: which way the normals or axes point. Default closest.

flip.description: mate: flip a distance or angle to the other side.

tools.name: sw_interference
tools.description: Check an assembly for parts that overlap: every interfering pair (or group) of components with the volume they share in mm3, largest first. Touching faces do not count unless touching is true. 0 interferences means nothing overlaps.

doc.description: Path, file name or title of an open assembly. Default: the active document.

touching.description: Count faces that only touch as interference too. Default false.

limit.description: At most this many interferences listed. Default 100.

tools.name: sw_bom
tools.description: Bill of materials of an assembly: each distinct file and configuration with its quantity and custom properties (configuration values override file values). mode parts (default) flattens sub-assemblies into the parts they contain; top counts the top-level components. Suppressed, envelope and excluded-from-BOM components are left out, as SOLIDWORKS does. With csv, also writes the table as a CSV file into the output folder (fetched into the workspace like an export).

doc.description: Path, file name or title of an open assembly. Default: the active document.

properties.description: Only these custom properties, in this column order. Default: all of them.

csv.description: Also write a CSV, e.g. bom.csv.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing CSV. Default false.

limit.description: At most this many rows in the answer (the CSV has all). Default 1000.

tools.name: sw_drawing
tools.description: Make a drawing of a saved part or assembly: a new drawing from the default (or given) template with the views laid out in projection (first or third angle, as the sheet says or as asked), at the largest standard scale that fits above the title block, and the model's dimensions brought in. The drawing stays open as a new document: sw_view shows it, sw_export writes it as PDF or DXF, sw_save with a .slddrw path keeps it.

doc.description: Path, file name or title of an open part or assembly with a file. Default: the active document.

scale.description: Sheet scale like 1:2 or 2:1. Default: the largest standard scale that fits.

dimensions.description: Bring in the model's dimensions. Default true.

template.description: Windows path of a .drwdot template. Default: the one set in SOLIDWORKS' options.

tools.name: sw_export
tools.description: Write a copy of a document in another format; the open document and its file stay as they are. The extension picks the format: .step .stp .igs .iges .x_t .x_b .sat .stl .pdf .dxf .dwg .eprt .easm .edrw .jpg .png .tif, or .sldprt .sldasm .slddrw for a native copy. A bare file name goes into the bridge's output folder; any other path must be inside a folder the bridge may write. Returns the Windows path, size and sha256.

doc.description: Path, file name or title of an open document. Default: the active document.

path.description: Target file, e.g. bracket.step or C:\out\bracket.step

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file. Default false.

sheets.description: Drawings to PDF: every sheet (default) or the active one.

tools.name: sw_save
tools.description: Save a document. With path: save it as that file, with its native extension (.sldprt, .sldasm, .slddrw), in the bridge's output folder or a folder it may write; the open document becomes that file and any original file stays as it was. This is how a document from sw_new or sw_drawing gets a file, and parts must have one before sw_assemble can use them. Without path: save over the document's own file, refused unless the bridge was started with saving enabled.

doc.description: Path, file name or title of an open document. Default: the active document.

path.description: Save as this file, e.g. bracket.sldprt (a bare name goes into the output folder).

overwrite.description: With path: replace an existing file. Default false.

tools.name: sw_close
tools.description: Close a document. A document with unsaved changes is closed only if the bridge opened it and discard is true; changes someone made by hand are never thrown away.

doc.description: Path, file name or title of an open document. Default: the active document.

discard.description: Throw away unsaved changes made through the bridge. Default false.

tools.name: sw_view
tools.description: A picture of the model as SOLIDWORKS renders it, zoomed to fit: one standard view, or several on one labelled contact sheet (e.g. front, top, right, isometric) so a single image shows the whole shape. display picks shaded, wireframe or hidden-line rendering. Returns a PNG. The user's view, display mode and active document are restored afterwards. Use it after every change you make to the geometry.

doc.description: Path, file name or title of an open document. Default: the active document.

view.description: One view. Default isometric. Drawings always render the current sheet.

views.description: Up to 6 views on one picture, instead of view.

display.description: How to render. Default: as the user has it.
